question: In the Dog Aging Project Precision Cohort survey of the plasma metabolome (first year of sampling), approximately what percentage of measured metabolites showed an effect of age?

evidence.title: Protein Catabolites as Blood-Based Biomarkers of Aging Physiology: Findings From the Dog Aging Project.
evidence.quote: We identified effects of age on approximately 36% of measured metabolites.

question: In the Dog Aging Project Precision Cohort plasma metabolome study that identified post-translationally modified amino acids (ptmAAs) as a novel biomarker of age, what clinical physiological measure mediated about half of the age effect on ptmAA levels, and was the ptmAA-age association robust to diet?
answer: Clinical measures of kidney function mediated about half of the age effect; yes, the ptmAA covariation with age was robust to diet.

evidence.title: Protein Catabolites as Blood-Based Biomarkers of Aging Physiology: Findings From the Dog Aging Project.
evidence.quote: The ptmAAs, which are generated by protein hydrolysis, covaried both with age and with other biomarkers of amino acid metabolism, and in a way that was robust to diet. Clinical measures of kidney function mediated about half of the age effect on ptmAA levels.

question: In the Dog Aging Project Precision Cohort targeted plasma metabolome study (the ptmAA biomarker paper), how many of the six measured carnitines associated strongly with age, and which was the only one negatively associated with age?
answer: 4 of the 6 carnitines; γ-butyrobetaine was the only one negatively associated with age (the other 3 were positively associated).

evidence.title: Protein Catabolites as Blood-Based Biomarkers of Aging Physiology: Findings From the Dog Aging Project.
evidence.quote: However, of the six carnitines measured, four associated strongly with age, with all but one, γ‐butyrobetaine, positively associated with age.

notes: Full-text discussion detail; the aqueous panel excluded hydrophilic lipids.

question: In the large-scale global metabolomic profiling of companion dogs of varying sizes and ages from three US cities, which factor gave the strongest signal in the metabolome, and after controlling for it, which metabolic pathway was associated with body weight and in which size class were its metabolites higher?
answer: Geographic location (stronger than age, breed or sex); tryptophan metabolism, with small dogs having significantly higher levels of tryptophan pathway metabolites.

evidence.title: Tryptophan metabolism is differently regulated between large and small dogs.
evidence.quote: We found a surprisingly strong location signal in the metabolome, stronger in fact than any signal related to age, breed, or sex. However, after controlling for the effects of location, tryptophan metabolism emerged as significantly associated with weight of the dogs, with small dogs having significantly higher levels of tryptophan pathway metabolites.

evidence.title: THE EFFECTS OF AGE AND SIZE ON THE COMPANION DOG METABOLOME: ROLES OF TRYPTOPHAN AND FATTY ACID METABOLISM
evidence.quote: After controlling for this location effect, we found a strong signal of amino acid metabolism, specifically tryptophan metabolism, associated with weight in the dog where metabolites in the tryptophan metabolism pathway were always higher in small, long-lived dogs.

question: In the year-long study comparing a fresh, human-grade food with an extruded kibble diet in 22 geriatric Alaskan sled dogs, which serum metabolite groups were decreased in the fresh-food (treatment) group?
answer: Advanced glycation end products, fatty acid synthesis, and creatinine.

evidence.title: Serum Metabolomics of Senior Dogs Fed a Fresh, Human-Grade Food or an Extruded Kibble Diet.
evidence.quote: The treatment group had decreased advanced glycation end products, fatty acid synthesis, and creatinine.

question: In the year-long serum metabolomics study of geriatric Alaskan sled dogs switched from extruded kibble to a fresh, human-grade food, when did the largest change in the serum metabolome occur relative to the rest of the year?
answer: Within the first month of consuming the treatment diet; changes over the rest of the year were modest by comparison.

evidence.title: Serum Metabolomics of Senior Dogs Fed a Fresh, Human-Grade Food or an Extruded Kibble Diet.
evidence.quote: There was a large change in the serum metabolome within the first month of consuming the treatment diet, with changes in the metabolome over the rest of the year being modest in comparison to the first month.

question: In the 24-week restricted-feeding study of a high-protein, high-fiber diet in 12 overweight spayed female dogs, what percentage of initial body weight was lost, and which two inflammatory markers decreased with weight loss?
answer: 31.2% of initial body weight; C-reactive protein and interleukin-6 decreased (along with triglycerides, leptin and insulin).

evidence.title: Weight loss and high-protein, high-fiber diet consumption impact blood metabolite profiles, body composition, voluntary physical activity, fecal microbiota, and fecal metabolites of adult dogs.
evidence.quote: After 24 wk, dogs lost 31.2% of initial BW and had 1.43 ± 0.73% weight loss per week. BCS decreased (P < 0.0001) by 2.7 units, fat mass decreased (P < 0.0001) by 3.1 kg, and fat percentage decreased (P < 0.0001) by 11.7% with weight loss. Many serum metabolites and hormones were altered, with triglycerides, leptin, insulin, C-reactive protein, and interleukin-6 decreasing (P < 0.05) with weight loss.

question: In the Dog Aging Project cross-sectional inflammaging pilot study of 47 healthy companion dogs of various breeds, which serum cytokines were positively associated with age, and which hematological parameter was negatively associated with age?
answer: IL-6, IL-8 and TNF-α were positively associated with age; lymphocyte count was negatively associated with age.

evidence.title: The companion dog as a model for inflammaging: a cross-sectional pilot study.
evidence.quote: Serum IL-6, IL-8, and TNF-α concentrations were all positively associated with age. Lymphocyte count was negatively associated with age.

question: In the preprint characterizing age-associated hematologic and serum cytokine profiles in intact laboratory Beagles, how many dogs were studied over what age span, and which sex showed extensive age-dependent inflammatory restructuring of cytokines?
answer: 80 intact laboratory Beagles spanning 1 to 11 years; intact males showed extensive age-dependent inflammatory restructuring, whereas females showed restricted fluctuations.

evidence.title: Sex-dimorphic immune trajectories across the canine lifespan and early-life signatures of geroprotective interventions
evidence.quote: Here, we characterize the age-associated hematologic and serum cytokine profiles of 80 intact laboratory Beagles spanning 1 to 11 years. Contrary to classical linear models of immunosenescence and inflammaging, we reveal that canine immune aging is highly dynamic and sexually dimorphic. While absolute leukocyte counts declined continuously, cytokine remodeling was sex-specific: intact males exhibited extensive age-dependent inflammatory restructuring, whereas females demonstrated restricted fluctuations.

question: In the Dog Aging Project Precision cohort gut microbiome study (over 900 dogs, fecal shotgun metagenomics), what kind of model did the age-associated gradual shifts in microbiome composition support developing, and which human cohort was used to test whether human age-associated microbial patterns are recapitulated in dogs?
answer: A metagenomics-based population-level model for canine age prediction from microbial signatures; the Lifelines-DEEP human cohort.

evidence.title: Mapping the canine gut microbiome: insights from the Dog Aging Project.
evidence.quote: In addition, we find age-associated gradual shifts in microbiome composition, supporting the development of a metagenomics-based population-level model for canine age prediction based on microbial signatures. We further examined which age-associated microbial patterns observed in humans are recapitulated in dogs by comparing our cohort with the Lifelines-DEEP cohort.

question: In the multi-omic study profiling whole-blood gene expression and plasma protein abundance in 40 laboratory beagles across young, old and geriatric life stages, how many genes and how many proteins significantly changed in abundance with aging, and on which pathways did they converge?
answer: 816 genes and 40 proteins; converging on DNA repair, collagen processing, and inflammation pathways.

evidence.title: Multi-omic analysis of canine aging uncovers conserved aging pathways.
evidence.quote: We identified 816 genes and 40 proteins that significantly changed in abundance during aging, converging on pathways involved in DNA repair, collagen processing, and inflammation.

question: In the immunophenotyping study of peripheral blood lymphocytes in 160 healthy dogs aged 1 to 17 years and 365 dogs with tumors, how did the CD4:CD8 ratio change with age in healthy dogs, and how did the ratio in tumor-bearing dogs compare with age-matched controls?
answer: It decreased significantly with age in healthy dogs, whereas dogs with tumors had a significantly higher CD4:CD8 ratio than age-matched controls.

evidence.title: Alterations of lymphocyte subpopulations in healthy dogs with aging and in dogs with cancer.
evidence.quote: The CD4:CD8 ratio showed a significant age-related decrease. In contrast, dogs with tumors possessed significantly lower absolute numbers and relative percentages of all lymphocyte phenotypes, while the CD4:CD8 ratio was significantly higher than in age-matched controls.

notes: Counter-intuitive detail: tumor-bearing dogs show a higher, not lower, CD4:CD8 ratio than age-matched controls.
